prompt:
I have a weird task for you. I want you to look at the app and create, for lack of a better word, a canvas that I can zoom in and zoom out and move around to see how our architecture actually works. A lot has changed, and I'm starting to lose an overview of everything that we're doing, especially with Model and Convex.

I want you to map out in a visual way what happens when a user signs up, pays, or gets a guest pass, and then they upload a file. What happens? We create, for example, right now. That's one of the things that I really want to understand. Right now, we're still creating a chat and a project, but the chats are actually independent, I believe, and the projects, I don't even know how the fuck that works. That's already where it starts.

A file is being uploaded, and then that file is being put somewhere into R2 storage, and then some modal workers are doing some things. There's a modal app, or one modal worker, but that has multiple apps. I don't really understand how that works either. I really want you to have a visualization of how this actually all works.

summary: Robin Ebers uses Claude Opus 5.5 to inspect an application codebase and generate an interactive, zoomable architecture diagram canvas that explains system data flows step by step.

post.originalText:
had a crazy idea today

for the past two months i've been building a pretty massive app

and truth be told, i often play catch-up on architecture, because features move so damn fast

so today i asked claude (opus 5.5, high)

"I have a weird task for you. I want you to look at the app and create, for lack of a better word, a canvas that I can zoom in and zoom out and move around to see how our architecture actually works."

(full prompt in first comment)

this came out pretty great and it truly visualized, with steps and connected graphs what everything does

10/10 would recommend

sourceMaterials.text: @aarondevs or, hear me out, run one prompt
sourceMaterials.author: robinebers

but am considering it

sourceMaterials.text:
@woodchipdaddy far too slow imo

ship fast
make it work
remove shit after

that's how most companies ship right now and the longer i do it myself, the more i realize why. lightspeed. yes you absolutely ship some slop. but you ship faster than ever and iterate faster too.
